chunks: Al-Yafi'i said in Mir'at al-Jinan, vol. 3, p. 28:

(The scholar of the Shia and the Imam of al-Rafida — possessor of many compositions, their Sheikh known as al-Mufid and also as Ibn al-Mu'allim, proficient in kalam, jadal, and fiqh; and he used to debate the people of every creed, with great majesty in the Buyid state...)

key_terms.التَّصَانِيفِ: tasānīf — scholarly compositions and authored works
key_terms.الْجَدَلِ: jadal — formal dialectics and scholarly disputation

ai.seo_question: What did the Sunni historian al-Yafi'i say about Sheikh al-Mufid in Mir'at al-Jinan?
ai.summary: Al-Yafi'i, a prominent Sunni Shafi'i historian, praises Sheikh al-Mufid in Mir'at al-Jinan (vol. 3, p. 28) as the foremost scholar of the Shia, known by the epithets al-Mufid and Ibn al-Mu'allim, mastering kalam, jadal, and fiqh and composing numerous works. Notably, al-Yafi'i — himself a Sunni — attests to al-Mufid's great prestige within the Buyid state and his regular engagement in open debate with adherents of every creed, making this passage a significant cross-sectarian testimonial to al-Mufid's intellectual stature.
